sourceNote: A copy of assets/models/dog/dog-patch.glb (armSource) with new quad tubes on each arm from the shoulder line to the wrist, 1.35 times longer than the arms of the source. tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py --factor 1.35 makes these faces. The other faces and dog-patch.glb stay unchanged.
armSourceNote: The dog mesh with one local edit (assets/models/dog/README.md). The faces that join each arm to the trunk below the cut top go, and a round patch of new vertices closes the inner side of each arm (tools/blender/arm_patch.py), so that the raised cello arms do not stretch the shoulder seam into flat shards. tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py reads it.
paintedNote: The weights of the clavicles and the arms are the automatic weights of Blender with the weight rules of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py. The vertices on the bones of paintedLower keep the rule weights, as on the monkey.

armSegments.note: Each upper arm and each forearm has 4 deform segments, and each elbow and wrist a helper bone. The helper is twice the gap of the elbow rings of tools/blender/arm_rebuild.py (step_skeleton() prints it).

name: Dog

app.note: The scale puts the standing head top at 1.570 m, the head top of the red fox: 1.433782 m for each unit, with the standing shoulder joints at 1.00078 m (ANIMALS). The reach goes from the shoulder joint to the middle of the palm.

armFactorNote: The factor 1 keeps the arm length, because the rig with arm segments does not stretch the arms. The arms of dog-arms.glb are 1.35 times longer than the arms of the source (arm_rebuild.py --factor 1.35), and the arm joints are the joints of the longer arms, so the reach stays app.reach: 0.4512 m (0.3464 m with no factor), 0.92 of the trunk, as the red fox. With the 1/2 cello of the dog (celloScale 0.86 of src/models/species.ts), the left paw reaches the whole fingerboard.
jointsNote: The places are in the studio units and axes of the source pose: 1 unit from the soles to the head top, +z forward, +x the left side. The tail is a chain of two bones. Each roll is the hint of the z axis of the bone.

studio.trunkNote: The trunk turns back by the share of each trunk bone until the hip angle opens by open degrees, with the shares of the cat. The trunk of the source leans 4.7 degrees forward from the hips joint to the neck joint.

tailCurl.note: The seated tail hangs down behind the seat between the back posts of the chair, with a soft bend, thinner than the source tail. The points are the curve after the tail root in the seated bind (curl_line() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). thin, blend, and smooth make a round thin tube.

studio.note: legTurns gives the world turn of each left leg bone from the seated bind to the source (tools/rig/leg_turns.py <config> 25 30 0): the thigh slopes 25 degrees down, and the shin is vertical. The thighs turn 30 degrees out, so that the knees spread around the lower bout of the cello.

weights.armIslandsNote: The round inner side of each arm of dog-patch.glb lies in part inside the plane armSplit, and only free arm vertices surround it. It follows the arm as the free arm beyond the plane (arm_islands() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py).

armRoot.note: After the cut, bone heat gives the free arm only arm weights, so the front of the right upper arm goes into the chest in the play. The inner root gives at most 0.25 of its arm weight to the chest. A higher share folds the cellist.

tail.radiusNote: The tail is the part of the mesh within 0.065 units of the line of the two tail bones. A larger radius takes a wide band of the rump, and the curl then bends it into a web between the back and the hanging tail.

sliver.note: The corners of each thin face share one set of weights, so that the face moves rigidly and does not turn over at a bent joint. The values are the values of the fox, the rabbit, and the cat.

line.note: The middle corner of each long thin face takes the mix of the weights of its two other corners by its place along their line. The values are the values of the fox and the cat.

weights.rigidNote: The corners of face 331 of the right armpit take the mean of their weights (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). The point is the middle of the face in the units of the source, at the plane of armSplit. With the mean, the face does not turn over.
weights.rigidPaintedNote: The faces at these points take the mean of the painted weights of their corners (rigid_faces() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py, after the painted weights): first two small faces that share two corners, then one thin face with a corner of 5 degrees. They lie at the right shoulder line of dog-arms.glb, where the cut plane of arm_rebuild.py passes 0.4 mm from a vertex of dog-patch.glb, and they turned over at rest on the bent bind (pnpm fold-probe cellist --faces).

haunch.note: The part of the thigh weight that goes to the hips grows from 0 at the lower height to 1 at the upper height, so that the buttocks stay on the hips. It starts 0.03 units above the knee and ends 0.03 units above the thigh joint.

earFlap.note: The long ears hang beside the head and the neck, below the head line. Each ear flap (the mesh below cut and farther than apart from the middle plane) follows the head and its ear bone, so that the head measures leave the flaps out.

weights.note: Beyond the plane |x| = armSplit, only the free arm follows the arm bones. Above headFrom (the chin), each vertex except the ear flaps follows the head only. The vertices within radius of the tail line and behind the plane z = behind follow the two tail bones.

cut.note: The cut removes the seam faces between the arm and the trunk, which stretch into flat shards when the cello arms rise. It ends above the shoulder joint (y 0.603). Each arm has a round patch in the mesh, so the cut closes only the trunk hole (open_loop() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py).

flip.note: The long edge of an arm face with a corner angle above angle (degrees) in the seated bind flips to the corner of the face on its other side, when the two faces lie almost on one plane and the surface moves at most move (units).

refine.ringsNote: The rig has no rings. pnpm rig-mesh dog --check lists the thin faces near the joints as candidates for a ring (check.thin). Rings at the elbows and the wrists fold the cellist more.

check.note: pnpm rig-mesh --check lists the faces of the seated bind with a corner angle below angle (degrees) and a longest edge of at least length (units), when that edge passes within near (units) of a joint of the arms or the legs. The values of the fox and the cat.

colors.note: The values of samples, palette, dark, and eyeShare are the values of the fox and the cat. A dark face in the eye box is an eye face. A face in the nose box that is nearer to the nose color than to white is a nose face and takes the gloss.

eyeShell.note: The values of the fox and the cat. The old eye of each side is its dark faces and the faces around them, and they take the color of the faces around them. No dark patch lies within darkReach, because the dark nose lies in front of the plane of the eyes.

chair.note: The seat is level, and its top is the lowest point of the seated body over the seat, with no shin, foot, or tail. The half width holds the haunch (x ±0.16). The front edge lies before the shins.

crease.note: The seated bind is smoothed across the crease where the belly meets the top of each thigh, with the values of the cat.

sit.note: The underside of the haunch behind the hip joints goes down onto the seat in the seated bind (sit() of tools/blender/rig_mesh.py). end, most, and smooth put the underside nearest to the seat top. root counts the root of the tail as the haunch, and top keeps the seat top fixed.

legFactorNote: The factor of the thigh and the shin: 1.5, the leg factor of the fox. With the thighs 25 degrees down and 30 degrees out, the seat of the legs is 0.266 m high at this scale.
